card.law_is_about: An ongoing bill revising energy-efficiency obligations, including annual savings by public bodies.
card.they_want: Explicitly recognise efficient hot-water fixtures as a public-sector energy-saving contribution.
card.they_claim: The EU requires new publicly owned buildings to be zero-emission from 1 January 2027.
card.the_problem: The enacted directive sets 1 January 2028; the submission advances that deadline by one year.

correction: Replace the claimed EU deadline with 1 January 2028. Article 7(1)(a) of the original adopted Directive (EU) 2024/1275 applies the zero-emission requirement to new buildings owned by public bodies from that date; other new buildings follow in 2030. This was already the adopted timetable when the 17 April 2026 submission was written.
effect: Makes the cited regulatory development one year less immediate, weakening a timing reason for adding explicit hot-water-efficiency recognition.
limits: Does not establish that recognising hot-water savings is unnecessary, that efficient fixtures fail to save energy, or that the underlying building-efficiency trend is false. The submission separately invokes existing savings potential and procurement clarity. The directive also permits specified exemptions, and national rules can be earlier or more stringent; the disputed sentence expressly attributes the 2027 date to the EU directive, rather than identifying an earlier German rule. A date slip is a plausible explanation, without any inference of intent.
materiality: Minor: one year changes the immediacy of an auxiliary regulatory reason, while the explicit request and independent savings arguments remain. This is not a claim about the size of realised savings.
direction_reasoning: The earlier deadline makes imminent public-building efficiency requirements appear more urgent, supporting the requested express recognition. This direction is assessed independently of the low materiality.

draft.title: Gesetz zur Beschleunigung der Umsetzung der Energieeffizienzrichtlinie
draft.relevant_provisions: Proposed section 6(1) and (3)–(4), physical pages 8–9, annual public-body savings and calculation of individual measures. The author identifies this exact draft on its first page; ministry 79-page PDF is byte-identical to archived version.
draft.version_limit: Register metadata lists dispatch on 9 April 2026, whereas the ministry-authored PDF itself is dated 17 April 2026. Do not infer a specific dispatch date from that conflict. Publication/registration in July–August does not substitute a later June Cabinet draft.
draft.process_status_at_screening: Ongoing parliamentary committee process; BT 21/8027, first reading 24 September 2026.

context_checks: Read all three pages and visually inspected page 1. The author explicitly names EPBD Directive (EU) 2024/1275 and immediately links higher building efficiency to the need to close a perceived hot-water gap before enactment.

Checked the original directive’s Article 7(1)(a) via official indexed full text, rather than relying on the later consolidated version alone. The Commission’s official zero-emission-building explanation independently confirms the same 2028 date.
Archived Council document 7532/24 records the Parliament’s March 2024 first-reading text and also shows 2028. It is corroboration, not mislabelled as the final Official Journal text.
Possible confusion with other EPBD deadlines, such as solar deployment by end-2026 or a January-2027 life-cycle roadmap, does not change the expressly described zero-emission-building obligation.
The April German energy-efficiency draft does not create the alleged January-2027 EPBD zero-emission standard; the disputed factual attribution concerns an already enacted EU text.
provenance: Primary three-page Hansgrohe submission extracted as official BMWE ZIP member 033; no mirror-only attribution. Official Lobbyregister SG2607300011 and R005487 link the same named request and three-page response to the exact ministry draft. The register PDF attachment could not be retrieved; no byte-identity claim is made between that attachment and the ministry member.
